Admin-controlled Jupyter and app startup

This silent recording uses disposable accounts and actual Jupyter/app servers. It shows separate startup approval and process restart controls. Gateway and worker pod replacement were tested separately, without manual service relaunch.

  1. Open Managed startup services in Admin overview.
  2. Start the approved Jupyter service in the selected user's No Internet environment.
  3. Start that user's approved application.
  4. Refresh to review supervisor-reported running status.
  5. Restart the supervised application and verify that it returns.

A new definition starts stopped. An administrator can stop it so it remains stopped across worker replacement. Saved workspaces and notebook files persist; unsaved kernel memory and unmanaged terminal jobs do not resume automatically.

Startup definitions are mounted read-only inside each private runtime. The supervisor does not receive gateway accounts, agent history mounts, launch tokens or model-key environment values. Apps still operate with their owner's runtime permissions.
